title: Clarification of the Hyalella azteca (Saussure, 1858) complex, with a redescription of Hyalella dentata Smith, 1874 and an updated key to North American species of the genus (Amphipoda: Hyalellidae)
content:
Abstract
Hyalella dentata Smith, 1874, a freshwater amphipod originally described from Colorado and other localities within the United States, is redescribed based on syntype material and freshly collected specimens from near its presumed type locality. The redescription is based on new information that significantly narrowed down the formerly vague type locality. Results of both morphological and molecular analyses place H. dentata within the genus, with a broad range spanning from Alaska south to Colorado and east to the Laurentian Great Lakes. Analyses reveal that individuals of this species possess significant variation in their dorsoposterior carinae, with molecularly identical individuals from the same location either possessing or lacking these carinae. We discuss the importance of variation in this character and the implications for the taxonomy of the genus Hyalella, including a basis for H. inermis Smith, 1874 to be synonymized with H. dentata. We also create a revised key to all known species of Hyalella from the Nearctic, neotropical Mexico, and the Caribbean. This key prioritizes characters that do not require dissection (whenever possible) and those showing morphological stability.
